A sphere subset enclosed by radius r<1 lies in a spherical cap, so any hull point has norm>=sqrt(1-r^2). This gives h_E(t)<=a(1-sqrt(1-t^2/b^2)) on [0,b]. The two boundary points a sqrt(1-t^2/b^2)e +- t f have Rad=t and midpoint on major axis. Direct constrained minimization of |xe-Av| over sphere, using b in the orthogonal part, shows nearest boundary distance a-x for x>=a-b^2/a, otherwise b sqrt(1-x^2/(a^2-b^2)). Equality thus persists exactly to t_star=(b^2/a)sqrt(2-b^2/a^2); compactness and equality rigidity give strict inequality to affine bound for nonround t>t_star. An antipodal minor-axis pair attains defect b at t=b, and the distance throughout the filled ellipsoid is <=b. Sphere a=b correctly joins regimes at t=b. Independent axis-witness tests on 20 cases corroborate threshold and strictness; proof controls all d and all (possibly infinite) subsets via compact Caratheodory.
